Subject: Springboard renewal & capacity add — redlines and ask

Hi Ethan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the conversation this week. Attached are the renewal draft MSA and an order form showing the proposed capacity increase (Q3 to Q4 uplift). High level asks from our side:

- Move from 12-month term to 24-month term (start date 2028-07-01)
- Add 30% seat/throughput uplift on the order form (see tab "proposed")
- Clarify SLA credits for sustained latency > 150ms P95 for 3 consecutive days

Marissa, we included a few redlines directly in the doc but flagged two clauses that require legal alignment: indemnity carveouts for third-party models and the data retention minimums for audit logs.

We'd like to get these finished this week if possible; Amelia and our procurement lead are available for a 30-min call Thu afternoon.

Amelia — got it, thanks for sending.

Quick notes:
- We're generally supportive of a 24-month term but need to confirm the rollover/termination mechanics for the capacity uplift. Our finance team usually asks for a phased billing schedule for large upticks.
- SLA credit language: we'll need to align on the measurement window (UTC vs local) and whether "sustained" means consecutive or rolling-window breaches.
- Indemnity: flagged to Marissa; we believe a scoped carveout for third-party model providers (open-source license exposure) is reasonable but want narrow language.

Marissa / legal — can you review the attached and call out the line numbers where you want different language? I've attached our standard renewal play (current_proposal.docx) with the billing cadence we typically propose.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Springboard renewal & capacity add — legal redlines and ask

Ethan / Amelia — I reviewed the draft and attached a marked-up version (MSA_redline_v2.docx). Summary of my change recommendations and open items below: 

1) Term / Termination:
- Accept 24-month term but add explicit language for pro-rated credits if customer reduces committed capacity within first 12 months.

2) Indemnity / Third-party models: 
- Reword narrow carveout to read: "Customer shall not seek indemnity from Provider for claims arising solely from Customer's deployment of third-party models where Provider has no proprietary modifications." (line 112-118)
- Add mutual notice window (30 days) for discovered license issues.

3) Data retention & audit logs:
- Can accept 18 months retention for audit logs, but we need a clause allowing export within 30 days for compliance audits.

4) SLA credits:
- Propose clarifying measurement in UTC and define "sustained" as "three consecutive reporting intervals (24-hour windows)". We can offer a cap of 10% monthly invoice credit for repeated breaches.

5) Order form: 
- Recommend phased billing schedule: 50% on renewal, 25% at month 6 of term, 25% at month 12 (to align spend with usage ramp). See attached note in OrderForm_2028_Q2.xlsx tab "billing_notes".

Open items for commercial to confirm: 
- Final uplift percentage (Amelia requested 30% — confirm whether that is committed or seasonal burst)
- Whether DocuSign path is acceptable for signatures or if Springboard requires signed PDFs with countersignature.

If we can get agreement on bullets above, I can produce an execution-ready MSA and accompanying amendment for signatures.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Amelia Chen <amelia@springboard.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Springboard Procurement <procurement@springboard.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Springboard renewal & capacity add — legal redlines and ask

Thanks, Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 30% uplift is a committed increase for Q4 (not seasonal) — we can lock that in on the order form.
- For indemnity, our counsel prefers the provider remain responsible when their managed model changes create downstream issues; your proposed narrow carveout sounds reasonable but can you add language about remediation timelines?
- DocuSign is acceptable. We can do the signature routing if you provide the final package.

I'll take the revised redline to our legal team this afternoon. Call at Thu 4pm PT still works for us — Amelia and our procurement director will join.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Amelia
